( Second Revision )
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part III/Set I ) ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 4 May 1979, after the draft finalized by the Sanitary Appliances and Water Fitrings Sectional by the Civil Engineering Division Committee had been approved Council. was first issued in 1958 and was revised in 1963 to for additional glazed earthenware sanitary appliances, such as Orissa pan, laboratory sink, squatting plate, slab and stall urinals In this revision the scope of the standard has and half-round channel. been restricted to cover requirements for glazed fire-clay sanitary appliances only since the glazed earthenware sanitary appliances were The Sectional Committee has found that outdated as well as unhygienic. only some of the sanitary appliances were being made in glazed fire-clay and therefore decided to cover the requirements for these appliances only The general requirements applicable to all appliances in this revision. and specific requirements for different types of appliances have been covered in separate parts of the standard. This standard ( Part III/Set 1) lays down the specific requirements of slab urinals. 0.2 This standard
cover requirements

Mark is governed by the provisions of the NOTE - The use of the Standard Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on proqucts covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS .and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
